selection_note: A bounded, no-cost, local-model live canary of the optional sf_heinlein stage. Exactly two stories: one expected to meet Heinlein's conditions and one negative control, each with an operational expectation recorded before any trial. The expectations are operational checks, not gold labels, and are not evidence of theoretical accuracy. Run with the Heinlein flag through a loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint only; see heinlein_canary_runbook.md.

expectations.rationale: The story posits an aging cure, a stabilized population, and voluntary termination as the standing conditions of its world. A father's triplets exceed the population quota, which is a human problem created by those conditions, so different, essential, human, and causal should all be present. Plausible is the only condition a model might reasonably mark ambiguous. Qualifies is allowed but not demanded, because a single local-model run varies.

A fairy tale in which an unexplained bell in a wood draws townspeople and children, resolved as an allegory of nature and poetry. It extrapolates no scientific or technological condition and its problem is not created by one, so the verdict should not be qualifies. It was also the negative control in the Knight and Suvin canary, which keeps the two canaries comparable.
